comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C1-C11. Both evaluations find the phenotypic observations (adhesion, migration, morphology defects in Tgif1-deficient cells) well-supported by rigorous in vitro and in vivo approaches. OpenEval emphasizes complementary experimental methods and statistical rigor; peer reviewers describe evidence as 'compelling' with no concerns raised.

Perfect agreement on claims C12-C16. Both evaluations support the spreading and focal adhesion findings. OpenEval highlights convergence of genetic and knockdown approaches; peer reviewers explicitly affirm decreased migration, abnormal morphology, and decreased focal adhesions with no concerns.

Agreement on negative findings (C17-C21) but different emphasis. OpenEval (covering C17-C31) views negative results as strengthening specificity of Pak3 mechanism. Peer review R3 (covering only C17-C21) explicitly acknowledges these negative findings as important for ruling out direct mechanisms, accepting them without critique.

Strong agreement on Tgif1-Pak3 mechanism (C22-C31 overlap). Both evaluations strongly support the novel transcriptional repression mechanism. OpenEval emphasizes multiple lines of evidence and functional rescue; peer reviewers describe this as 'the first study to identify' this mechanism with 'well supported and justified' conclusions.

Agreement on ERK1/2 and PTH regulation of Tgif1 (C32-C39 overlap). OpenEval (covering C32-C46) emphasizes time-course data and pathway-specific inhibitors; peer review R5 (covering C32-C39) explicitly affirms time-dependent regulation through various experimental approaches with no critique.

Agreement on Tgif1 promoter regulation (C40-C46 overlap). OpenEval highlights promoter truncation analysis and AP1 involvement; peer review R6 accepts the promoter mapping and AP1 mechanism as part of the overall regulatory framework with no concerns raised.

Perfect agreement on fracture healing claims C47-C48. Both evaluations support the in vivo fracture healing data. OpenEval notes appropriate caveats about osteoclast contribution; peer reviewers explicitly confirm impaired healing findings and note that prior concerns about in vivo data were addressed in revisions.

Perfect agreement on PTH response claims C49-C52. Both evaluations support the histomorphometric findings in germline and conditional knockouts. OpenEval emphasizes cell autonomy demonstration; peer reviewers explicitly affirm impaired PTH-induced osteoblast activation with no concerns.

Perfect agreement on PTH-Tgif1-PAK3 axis claims C53-C61. Both evaluations strongly support the mechanistic link. OpenEval highlights epistatic relationship through double knockdown; peer reviewers describe this as a 'novel finding' that advances understanding of osteoblast migration with 'compelling' evidence.

Perfect agreement on integrative conclusions C62-C64. Both evaluations affirm the overall mechanistic pathway is well-supported. OpenEval emphasizes collective evidence from multiple approaches; peer reviewers state conclusions are 'well supported and justified' and that work 'substantially advances understanding.'

OpenEval evaluated background/contextual claims C65-C72 as appropriately supported by literature citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims, which is typical as peer reviewers focus on novel findings rather than established literature context.
